# The pms command line

<p class="pm-kind"><b>Reference · generated</b> · every subcommand and flag of `pms`, printed by the binary itself</p>

## `pms`

Sends, receives, encodes, and inspects pulses across the local mesh. Run `pms demo` first to see a producer + consumer talk through the mesh in one terminal.

### `pms doctor`

Verify the local toolchain and mesh runtime preconditions

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--for <FOR>` |  | Filter checks by developer profile (e.g. hft, ai, robotics) |

### `pms send`

Send pulses to a UDP destination

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<DEST>` | required | Destination address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:9000) |
| `--count <COUNT>` | `1` | Number of pulses to send |
| `--payload <PAYLOAD>` | `16` | Envelope payload size in bytes |

### `pms recv`

Bind a UDP address and print received pulses

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<BIND>` | required | Local bind address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:9000) |
| `--count <COUNT>` | `1` | Maximum pulses to receive before exiting |
| `--timeout-ms <TIMEOUT_MS>` | `5000` | Per-recv timeout in milliseconds |
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON instead of human-readable output |

### `pms version`

Print workspace + codec version stamp

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON instead of human-readable output |

### `pms encode`

Encode a JSON envelope spec and report the canonical wire bytes

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json <FILE>` | required | Path to a JSON spec file (schema: `EnvelopeSpec` in `pulse_cli::commands::encode_decode`) |
| `--json-out` |  | Emit JSON instead of human-readable output |

### `pms decode`

Decode canonical wire hex back into an envelope summary.

Exits with status 1 when the envelope does not verify: its content does not produce the identifier it carries.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<HEX>` | required | Hex string (whitespace trimmed) |
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON instead of human-readable output |

### `pms ring`

Snapshot a SHM-backed PulseRing (read-only secondary reader)

#### `pms ring inspect`

Snapshot ring header + the N most-recent slot summaries

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | required | Hub name (e.g. `default_hub`) or a raw POSIX SHM name starting with `/`; the ring's header gives its capacity |
| `--count <COUNT>` | `8` | Number of most-recent slots to summarize |
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON |

### `pms modules`

List the M01..M12 optimization modules, optionally by profile

#### `pms modules ls`

List modules, optionally filtered by developer profile

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--for <PROFILE>` |  | Filter by profile (hft, ai, robotics, telemetry, dev) |
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON |

### `pms bench`

Throughput and latency of pulses over UDP loopback on this host

#### `pms bench smoke`

Throughput and latency of pulses over UDP loopback on this host: the same run as `pulse bench`

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--count <COUNT>` | `10000` | Number of pulses to send through the loopback |
| `--json` |  | Emit JSON |

### `pms start`

Start the local `mesh-hub` daemon (UDS + WebSocket).

In the background (the default) it waits up to 60 s for the daemon to serve, and stops one that does not (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 5 s later) before it reports the failure and exits 1.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--foreground` | `false` | Run in the foreground (block until ^C) |
| `--basket-path <BASKET_PATH>` |  | Optional basket path for envelope capture |

### `pms attach`

Attach to a running mesh-hub daemon under the given name and park

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<NAME>` | required | Process-visible name to register under |

### `pms push`

Publish a one-shot envelope to a channel

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<CHANNEL>` | required | Routing key |
| `<PAYLOAD>` | required | Payload as a UTF-8 string. Use `--hex` for raw bytes via hex |
| `--hex` |  | Interpret `payload` as hex-encoded bytes |
| `--type-name <TYPE_NAME>` |  | Optional type name |

### `pms tap`

Subscribe to a channel and print events live

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--channel <CHANNEL>` |  | Channel filter (exact or glob). Default: all |
| `--type-name <TYPE_NAME>` |  | Type-name filter |
| `--json` |  | One JSON object per event instead of the table format |

### `pms hello`

Spin up a 2-thread demo (send + recv on channel `hello`)

### `pms demo`

One-command end-to-end smoke loop: auto-starts the daemon if needed, runs a 5-message producer/consumer demo, cleans up.

It exits 1, saying how many arrived, when fewer than all five messages reach the consumer within 5 s. With `PMS_DAEMON` set it uses the daemon that names and starts none.

### `pms keys`

Make and read the Ed25519 keys a client proves at attach.

A key file is its owner's alone (mode 0600), and a client refuses one its group or others may read or write. Each subcommand prints the key's public half as a line of a daemon's `--attach-keys` list: its standard base64, 44 characters.

#### `pms keys generate`

Write a new key to a new file, readable and writable by its owner alone, and print its public key.

Exits 1, replacing nothing, when the file exists or cannot be written.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | required | The key file to create |

#### `pms keys public`

Print the public key of a key file.

Exits 1 when the file cannot be read, holds no key, or its group or others may read or write it.

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | required | The key file to read |
